# Solar Eclipse Workbench script - total solar eclipse of 12 August 2026
# Generated by scripts/generate_20260812_EOS800D.py - edit that, not this file.
#
# Camera : Canon EOS 800D (max shutter 1/4000, ISO 100-25600)
# Optics : 80/480 mm refractor, fixed f/6 - the aperture column is informational,
#          the body cannot drive a telescope's aperture and the value is ignored.
# Filter : ND 4.0 photographic solar film for every partial-phase frame.
#
# Site   : Palencia, N Spain  42.0095 N, -4.5289 E, 740 m
# Type   : Total, magnitude 1.0119, totality 101 s
#
#   C1     17:33:56 UTC   sun  18.9 deg
#   C2     18:29:10 UTC   sun   8.7 deg
#   MAX    18:30:00 UTC   sun   8.6 deg
#   C3     18:30:51 UTC   sun   8.4 deg
#   C4     19:22:34 UTC   sun  -0.8 deg
#   sunset 19:22:53 UTC
#
# This is a sunset eclipse.  Totality happens at only 8.6 degrees altitude and the sun
# sets 19 s after C4, so the last partial phases are shot straight into the horizon haze.
# A clear, low western horizon matters more than anything else at this site.
#
# Atmospheric dimming
# -------------------
# Exposures are not constant through the eclipse: the sun drops from 18.9 deg at C1
# to the horizon, and airmass rises from 3.1 to over 30.  Every filtered frame below
# was computed for the sun altitude at that exact instant:
#   - above 5 deg : Jubier exposure tables, interpolated in sun altitude and site height
#   - below 5 deg : the tables break down, so the 5 deg value is extrapolated with a
#                   Kasten-Young airmass and 0.25 mag/airmass extinction.
# That extinction coefficient is a guess (0.15 clear .. 0.40 hazy), and the error grows
# to several stops at the horizon - hence the wide HDR brackets after C3+18m.
#
# Warning: at f/6 with ND 4.0 the early partials want 1/6400, which the 800D cannot do.
# Those frames are capped at 1/4000 and will be ~2/3 stop over - recoverable in RAW, but
# an extra 1-stop ND (or ND 5.0 film) would be better.  Shoot RAW.
#
# Comments carry the sun altitude and airmass X used for each exposure.

# --- Set-up and focus, before C1 (solar filter ON) ---
sync_cameras, C1, -, 0:20:00.0, "Sync camera clock and settings"
take_picture, C1, -, 0:15:00.0, Canon EOS 800D, 1/4000, 6.3, 100, "Focus check, uneclipsed disc (sun 21.7 deg, X=2.7)"
take_picture, C1, -, 0:10:00.0, Canon EOS 800D, 1/4000, 6.3, 100, "Focus check, uneclipsed disc (sun 20.8 deg, X=2.8)"
take_picture, C1, -, 0:05:00.0, Canon EOS 800D, 1/4000, 6.3, 100, "Framing check, uneclipsed disc (sun 19.8 deg, X=2.9)"
take_hdr, C1, -, 0:03:00.0, Canon EOS 800D, 1/4000, 6.3, 100, 4, "Exposure-check bracket, four stops down from the fastest speed the body has"
sync_cameras, C1, -, 0:01:30.0, "Re-sync before the eclipse starts"

# --- TOTALITY (101 s, sun 8.6 deg - FILTER OFF) ---
# Ladder: 1/1600, 8 stops down and back = 17 frames at ISO 400.
# Three identical ladders so the corona can be stacked, with the window around
# maximum filled by deep ISO 800 outer-corona frames.  The 1 s and 1.6 s frames
# need the mount tracking at 480 mm.
#
# Throughput: the 800D holds ~21 RAW frames of buffer and sustains roughly 1.5
# frames/s to a fast UHS-I card.  Every camera command here takes a per-camera USB
# lock and is DROPPED if it cannot get it within 1.5 s (camera.py _MAX_LOCK_WAIT_S),
# so an overrunning ladder deletes whatever is scheduled next rather than running
# late.  The bursts and ladders below are sized to stay under that: 110 frames in
# totality, 1.1 frames/s and ~29 MB/s to the card.
voice_prompt, C2, -, 0:00:00.0, C2, "Second contact - filters off, totality has begun"
take_burst, C2, -, 0:00:03.0, Canon EOS 800D, 1/3200, 6.3, 100, 3, "Diamond ring and Baily's beads at C2"

take_picture, C2, +, 0:00:05.5, Canon EOS 800D, 1/800, 6.3, 100, "Prominences"
take_hdr, C2, +, 0:00:07.0, Canon EOS 800D, 1/1600, 6.3, 400, 8, "Corona ladder A"
take_hdr, C2, +, 0:00:26.0, Canon EOS 800D, 1/1600, 6.3, 400, 8, "Corona ladder B"
